units.source_text: 这个女子谈到小说的事，听起来仿佛同日常所用的“文学”两字毫不相关。

en.t: When this woman talked about novels, it sounded as though they had nothing at all to do with the everyday word “literature.”

units.source_text: 看来这村庄人们之间的情谊，也只是交换着看看妇女杂志而已，除此之外，就完全是孤孤单单地各看各的书了。

en.t: It seemed that her ties with the people of this village amounted only to exchanging women’s magazines to read; apart from that, everyone read books in complete solitude.

units.source_text: 没有选择，也不求甚解，只要在客栈的客厅等处发现小说或杂志，借来就翻阅。

en.t: She chose nothing in particular and did not seek any deep understanding; whenever she found novels or magazines in the inn’s parlor or some such place, she borrowed them and leafed through them.

units.source_text: 她凭记忆所列举的新作家的名字，有不少是岛村所不知道的。

en.t: Among the names of new writers she listed from memory, quite a few were ones Shimamura did not know.

units.source_text: 听她的口气，像是在谈论遥远的外国文学，带着一种凄凉的调子，同毫无贪欲的叫化子一样。

en.t: From her tone, it was as if she were speaking of some distant foreign literature, with a desolate note like that of a beggar free of all greed.

units.source_text: 岛村心想：这恐怕同自己凭借洋书上的图片和文字，幻想出遥远的西方舞蹈的情况差不多吧。

en.t: Shimamura thought: perhaps it was much the same as his own imagining of distant Western dance from the pictures and words in foreign books.
